translation: Huangfu Shi'an's 《Jiayi Jing》 (Systematic Classic of Acupuncture) especially valued needling and had no formulas; Chao Yuanfang's 《Bingyuan》 (Sources of Disease) had a source for every disease, and every source established a discourse, but had no formulas. Those who read them all regretted the lack of formulas. When it reached the Tang dynasty, there was the Perfected Sun (Sun Simiao), who first wrote thirty volumes of formulas and later added another thirty, cherishing his formulas and calling them the 《Qianjin》 (Thousand Golden Prescriptions); the medical formulas were comparatively clear and complete, being the great school.
